question: Which specific manufacturers are approved by the MUTCD to supply retroreflective sign sheeting?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not approve, endorse, or list any specific manufacturers of retroreflective sign sheeting, and none are named anywhere in the evidence provided. Instead, the Manual establishes performance-based requirements — for example, minimum maintained retroreflectivity levels in Table 2A-5, organized by sheeting types defined by the ASTM D4956 material standard — leaving the choice of supplier to the agency, so long as the material meets those performance criteria. Standards (mandatory): - "Regulatory signs shall be retroreflective or illuminated (see Section 2A.21)." — a performance requirement, with no manufacturer specified. - "Requirements for retroreflection of the red circle and diagonal shall be the same as those requirements for backgrounds, legends, symbols, arrows, and borders." — again, a performance requirement independent of any product brand. Options (permitted): - Highway agencies may exclude certain signs (Parking/Standing/Stopping R7–R8 series; Walking/Hitchhiking/Crossing R9 series and R10-1 through R10-4b; Acknowledgment signs; and bikeway signs intended exclusively for bicyclists or pedestrians) from the retroreflectivity maintenance guidelines — a decision framed around sign categories and performance, not around approved vendors. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-5, which specifies minimum maintained retroreflectivity levels (in cd/lx/m²) by sign color and by generic ASTM D4956 sheeting type (beaded Types I, II, III and prismatic), with no manufacturer names. [Image 5] (Page 44 context) and the related provisions discuss retroreflection of sign elements by generic means (e.g., "a material that has a smooth, sealed outer surface over a microstructure that reflects light"), not branded products. Citations: - Section 2B.01 Standard §3 (p.67) - Section 2M.07 Standard §2 (p.523) - Section 2A.22 Option §5 (p.63) - Section 2A.22 Option §4 (p.63) - Table 2A-5 (p.62)
